findings.title: New feature added without updating the approved help-output snapshots
findings.body: Adding `ROLLING_UPDATES` changes the list of possible values printed by `--features` and `--features-disabled` in every command's help. The Quarkus `HelpCommandDistTest` compares that output against static `*.approved.txt` snapshot files, and none of them are updated in this PR. Adding `rolling-updates:v1` to the feature list should make those approval tests fail. Regenerate and commit the approved help files, along with any other test that hard-codes the preview feature list.

findings.title: Docs say the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but nothing enforces it
findings.body: The new CAUTION says the `rolling-updates` feature must be enabled or the Operator will fail. This PR adds no Operator validation that inspects the CR's enabled features. The `ROLLING_UPDATES` enum constant is new here, so no earlier check could reference it. The Operator also does not run the `update-compatibility` commands in this version; the only update strategy is Recreate (or unset). So setting `spec.update.strategy: Recreate` without the feature still works, and the documented failure never happens. `UpgradeTest` enables the feature only when a strategy is set and never covers the claimed failure. Either add a reconcile-time validation that reports an error status when `spec.update` is used without the feature, or correct the documentation.

findings.title: Appending `--features=rolling-updates` to every documented command overrides the user's feature configuration
findings.body:
The `updatecompatibility` macro now hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates` on every documented invocation. A CLI option takes precedence over keycloak.conf and env, so any features the user already enables (e.g. `features=token-exchange` in the config file) are replaced for that run. That contradicts the guide's warning that the command must be run with exactly the same configuration as the deployment. A user who also passes their own `--features` gets a duplicate option.

`features` is also a build-time option. With an optimized/pre-built image (`--optimized`, which these commands support via `OptimizedMixin`), a runtime `--features` value is not applied. The check then reads the build-time profile and exits with "feature disabled" unless the image was built with the feature, as the PR itself does in `Dockerfile-custom-image`.

The docs should tell users to add `rolling-updates` to their existing feature list and to include it at build time for optimized images.

findings.title: Feature-gate and new exit codes are not asserted
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only exercises the `metadata` subcommand and only checks the error text. It never asserts the documented exit code 4 (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`), and the `check` subcommand's gate is not tested at all. The PR also changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and gives 4 a new meaning, yet `testWrongVersions` never asserts the exit code. A regression mixing up these two values, which callers rely on to choose a rolling vs. recreate strategy, would go unnoticed. Add `assertEquals(...exitCode())` checks for the disabled-feature case on both subcommands and for the incompatible-version case.
